h1: Duravit bathroom installation in Stoke Poges

hero.intro: A good number of the bathroom projects we take on in Stoke Poges involve more than one room at once — often a second en-suite being added off a principal bedroom, alongside work to an existing family bathroom, taking advantage of the sizeable gardens and set-back plots that are typical of the village's older period detached houses and newer executive-style builds alike. When a Duravit specification runs across more than one bathroom in the same house, the installation route needs to be consistent: a wall-hung pan going onto Duravit's own DuraSystem frame in one room and a standard concealed cistern frame in another is a decision worth making once, deliberately, rather than room by room. Duravit sanitaryware is something we fit regularly in and around Stoke Poges — a SensoWash shower toilet seat in one room, a full ME by Starck suite running across two or three — and the village's larger properties generally give us the room to plan that consistently across a multi-room project.

sections.heading: Duravit across a multi-room project
sections.body: Where a Stoke Poges project covers two or three bathrooms rather than one, we see Duravit specified across the whole house more often than not — the same ME by Starck suite in a principal en-suite and a family bathroom, for example, or a SensoWash shower toilet seat in one room and a standard WC pan in another. We're fit-only throughout: you choose and supply the Duravit sanitaryware, brassware and furniture for each room, and we coordinate the strip-out, frame installation, first fix, tiling and plumbing across the whole project rather than treating each bathroom as a separate job.

sections.heading: One frame decision, made early
sections.body: The detail to settle before any of it is ordered is the frame. Duravit's own DuraSystem frame suits some wall-hung pans, while others are compatible with a standard concealed cistern frame — the two aren't interchangeable once a stud wall is boarded and tiled. On a project spanning a new en-suite and an existing bathroom, we confirm the frame route for each room at survey stage, taking account of what's already in the existing bathroom's stud wall versus the blank slate a new en-suite off a principal bedroom usually offers, so the approach is consistent rather than decided piecemeal as each room is tackled.

sections.heading: Fit-only, from survey to snagging
sections.body: We work fit-only across Stoke Poges: you source the Duravit sanitaryware, brassware, tiles and furniture, and we strip out, first-fix, tile, plumb and snag, from £3,500 per bathroom. A £125 survey covers every room in a multi-bathroom project, confirming the frame route and layout for each one before anything is ordered, so a new en-suite and an existing family bathroom end up fitted to the same standard.

faqs.q: Can you fit Duravit across more than one bathroom in the same project?
faqs.a: Yes — it's common in Stoke Poges, where a new en-suite off a principal bedroom is often added alongside work to an existing bathroom. We coordinate the frame route and installation across every room in the project.

faqs.q: What's the difference between the DuraSystem frame and a standard concealed cistern frame?
faqs.a: DuraSystem is Duravit's own frame for some wall-hung pans; others are compatible with a standard concealed cistern frame. They aren't interchangeable once a wall is boarded, so we confirm the right one for each room before any stud wall goes up.

faqs.q: Do you supply the Duravit sanitaryware, or do I need to buy it?
faqs.a: We're fit-only, so you source the Duravit products — typically through a showroom — and we handle strip-out, frame installation, first fix, tiling and plumbing.

faqs.q: Does Stoke Poges' plot size make a multi-bathroom Duravit project easier?
faqs.a: Generally yes. The larger plots and set-back houses typical of Stoke Poges tend to give more room to add a new en-suite from scratch, which makes it easier to plan a consistent frame route across a project than in a more constrained property.

faqs.q: What does Duravit installation cost in Stoke Poges?
faqs.a: From £3,500 per bathroom, fit-only. A £125 survey confirms the frame route and scope for each room before we quote.

image.heroPrompt: Purpose: hero image for the Duravit x Stoke Poges installer page, implying Duravit's wall-hung WC and frame system through a construction-stage detail shot, relevant to the multi-bathroom projects typical of the town. Subject and action: a close mid shot of a wall-hung WC pan test-fitted against its concealed cistern frame inside an open timber stud wall, flush pipe and waste connection visible, pan not yet grouted or sealed. Setting and work-stage: a part-built en-suite off a principal bedroom in a Stoke Poges house, early evening, a single clamp work-light positioned to one side providing the main light source. Composition: close-to-mid angle square-on to the frame and pan, stud timber and a folded dust sheet visible at the edges of frame, pan and frame sharply focused in the centre. Light and materials: Calacatta marble floor tile laid but not yet grouted in front of the stud wall, brushed nickel waste and flush fittings on the frame, warm directional light from the single clamp lamp creating an uneven pool of light across the pan with the stud timber falling into shadow at the frame edges. Constraints: no people, no text, no logos, no brand names visible on fixtures, no LED strip lighting anywhere in frame, no catalog-symmetrical staging, no uniform amber wash across the whole frame — light should stay localised to the lamp's throw, no plants, florals or candles as props, no water shown running, varied sheen on the ungrouted marble tile with visible grout gaps rather than a finished uniform floor.
image.heroAlt: A Duravit-style wall-hung WC pan test-fitted against its concealed cistern frame on ungrouted Calacatta marble tile, warm work-light, part-built Stoke Poges en-suite.
